OFFICE MANAGER (ANZSCO 512111)
Full-Time | Adelaide, South Australia
Salary: $75,000 – $95,000 + Superannuation

About Bide With Care Pty Ltd
Bide With Care Pty Ltd (BWC) is a registered NDIS provider committed to delivering high-quality disability and aged care support services across South Australia. We provide person-centred care tailored to participant goals, independence, dignity, and wellbeing.
Our services include disability support, community participation, in-home care, personal care, supported accommodation, and aged care services. Due to continued business growth and increasing operational demands, we are seeking an experienced and highly organised Office Manager to oversee our office administration, operational systems, compliance functions, and staff coordination.

About the Role
The Office Manager is responsible for organising and controlling the administrative functions and resources of the office, including office systems, administrative staff, operational workflows, compliance systems, and business support functions.
This role plays a critical leadership function in ensuring efficient daily operations, regulatory compliance, workforce coordination, and continuous business improvement.

Key Responsibilities
Office Operations & Service Planning
•	Oversee daily office operations and administration functions to ensure smooth and efficient service delivery.
•	Contribute to the planning and review of office services, priorities, and service standards.
•	Develop, implement, and improve administrative systems, workflows, and reporting structures.
•	Drive accountability, workflow visibility, and operational efficiencies.
Resource Allocation & Staff Coordination
•	Allocate human resources, office space, equipment, and operational resources effectively.
•	Assign work to administrative staff and monitor work performance.
•	Coordinate operational communication between support workers, coordinators, nurses, and management.
•	Support workforce planning, scheduling, and resource allocation.
Compliance & Records Management
•	Manage company records, participant documentation, and office filing systems.
•	Maintain service agreements, incident reports, risk assessments, compliance registers, and internal records.
•	Ensure documentation complies with NDIS Practice Standards and Quality & Safeguards requirements.
•	Support preparation for audits, regulatory reporting, and compliance reviews.
Financial & Accounts Administration
•	Assist with accounts payable and receivable functions.
•	Manage invoices, purchase orders, reconciliations, and payment processing.
•	Assist with payroll coordination and financial administration.
•	Support budgeting and expenditure monitoring.
Operational Liaison & Problem Resolution
•	Liaise with healthcare professionals, participants, families, and external stakeholders to coordinate business operations.
•	Facilitate prompt resolution of operational, compliance, and administrative issues.
•	Support management with business planning and operational improvement initiatives.
Human Resources Coordination
•	Coordinate onboarding, recruitment support, staff induction, and compliance documentation.
•	Maintain HR records, staff training registers, and performance documentation.
•	Assist with personnel activities including hiring, performance management, payroll coordination, and supervision.
WHS & Legislative Compliance
•	Ensure compliance with occupational health and safety regulations.
•	Maintain workplace safety records and risk management systems.
•	Ensure operations comply with relevant legislation, government regulations, and internal policies.

Essential Skills & Experience
•	Diploma, Advanced Diploma, Associate Degree or higher in Business Administration, Management, Office Administration, or related field.
OR
•	Minimum three years’ relevant experience in office management or business administration.
•	Strong leadership and organisational skills.
•	Demonstrated experience managing office systems and administration functions.
•	Experience managing records, compliance systems, and operational workflows.
•	Strong financial administration and reporting capability.
•	Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.

Desirable
•	Experience in disability services, aged care, healthcare, or community services.
•	Knowledge of NDIS compliance and regulatory frameworks.
•	Experience in rostering and workforce coordination.

Why Join BWC?
•	Work with a growing and reputable NDIS provider.
•	Join a supportive and purpose-driven team.
•	Opportunity to contribute to meaningful outcomes for participants.
•	Leadership role with career growth opportunities.
If you are a highly motivated and experienced professional looking to contribute to operational excellence in a growing care organisation, we encourage you to apply.

Location: Palmerston, Northern Territory
Employment type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week
Salary: $67,510 to $72,000 plus superannuation

About us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the business
The business (ABN 91 213 951 452) is a takeaway food outlet located in a busy shopping centre food court in Palmerston, serving a range of freshly prepared takeaway meals, including loaded chips, fish and chips, fried chicken, seafood baskets, hotdogs, ice cream and milkshakes.

The successful applicant will oversee the outlet's front-of-house retail operations and support its smooth daily operation. 

About the Role
The Retail Supervisor will supervise and coordinate the activities of staff, maintain high customer service standards and assist management with staff supervision, stock control, cash handling and the day-to-day operation of the outlet. 

The position requires availability across a rotating roster, including weekends, public holidays and evening shifts where required.

Key Responsibilities
- Supervise and coordinate the daily activities of counter and staff.
- Allocate duties and prepare or assist with staff rosters.
- Ensure customers receive prompt, friendly and accurate service.
- Train staff in customer service, point-of-sale procedures, food handling and workplace requirements.
- Monitor staff performance and provide day-to-day guidance and support.
- Respond to customer enquiries, concerns and complaints.
- Operate and supervise point-of-sale and cash-handling procedures.
- Complete opening and closing procedures, including cash reconciliation.
- Monitor stock levels and assist with stocktaking and ordering.
- Receive and check deliveries against orders.
- Ensure menu items, promotional materials and prices are correctly displayed.
- Maintain the cleanliness and presentation of the service counter, customer areas and retail displays.
- Ensure food safety, workplace health and safety, security and hygiene procedures are followed.
- Report staffing, stock, equipment and operational issues to management.
- Assist with counter service and other operational duties during busy periods.

Skills and Experience
The successful applicant must have:
- At least one year of relevant experience in retail, takeaway food, fast food or a similar customer-service environment;
- Previous experience supervising or coordinating staff;
- Experience with point-of-sale systems, cash handling and daily reconciliations;
- Good customer service and complaint-handling skills;
- The ability to organise staff and prioritise duties during busy service periods;
- Knowledge of stock control and basic inventory procedures;
- Good communication and interpersonal skills;
- A reliable, organised and hands-on approach to work; and
- The ability to work weekends, public holidays and shifts according to the business roster.
- A current food-safety or food-handling certificate is desirable.

How to Apply
To apply, submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
- A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a busy and growing takeaway food business serving the Palmerston community, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 20 August 2026

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

We are looking for a special kind of person - a St Vincent's kind of person. Someone who puts compassion, connection and caring for other people at the heart of everything they do.

As a Casual Care Services Employee, you'll be part of an experienced, engaged and dedicated team helping to create a welcoming, professional and supportive care experience for the residents of St Vincent's Care Services, Yennora.

St Vincent's Care Services Yennora (locally known as Rosary Village) is a 141-bed facility located approximately 29km from Sydney's CBD.

At St Vincent's Care, our Heartprint model ensures compassionate, holistic, person-centred care that empowers residents and fosters a sense of belonging, independence, and cultural respect, creating a life filled with purpose and wellbeing.

We are seeking people who are passionate about providing care that is sensitive to resident's individualised needs, preferences and choices and are committed to building strong, meaningful connections with residents.

What's on your resume is important, but what's in your heart matters more.
Because at St Vincent's, kindness works for us.

Things that work for us:

Certificate III in Individual Support-Aged Care or similar qualifications essential.

6 months+ experience in a similar role with residential aged care experience highly regarded.

Availability to work minimum 3 shifts - AM, PM or Nights through the week.

Excellent customer service and communication skills.

Experience with AutumnCare (or similar software) with ability to maintain excellent records.

Understanding of Aged Care, resident rights-responsibilities with ability to follow the care plan.

Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check and NDIS Worker Screening Check will be a requirement of this role.

Things that work for you:

Competitive salary packaging options up to $15,990, Novated leasing, plus an optional Meals and Entertainment card up to $2,650 per annum

Opportunity to work for the nation's largest Catholic not-for-profit health and aged care provider, with a rapidly growing and progressive vision

Friendly team environment with a great community care spirit

Ability to visibly see your impact on the business and its service

No cost uniforms and training

Free annual flu vaccination

Employee Assistance Program for staff and their families

Access to the Fitness Passport (FP)

Why become part of the St Vincent's Care family?

Because you're like us, you believe that every act of kindness makes the world a better place. Better for everyone who lives in the 20+ facilities and locations we operate in Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria. Better for all our staff and employees, who work tirelessly to provide the highest levels of care and quality of life for our clients. And better support for the local communities we play an important role in and continue to support.

For more than 175 years, St Vincent's Care Services (SVCS) has been a leading Catholic provider of Aged Care Services in Australia, and the legacy of compassion, justice, integrity and excellence entrusted to us by the Sisters of Charity and their Founder Mary Aitkenhead continues to inspire our work today.

Our spiritual and hospital-based heritage has taught us that wellness is about more than medical needs. It's about building a true partnership around trust and respect. That's why we take a person-centred approach - delivering holistic, individual care that achieves wellbeing for mind, body and spirit.

At St Vincent's we value inclusivity and diversity and acknowledge the important of creating a work environment that is welcome, safe, fair and impartial and invite people from all backgrounds to join our caring family.

St Vincent's Health Australia embraces Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people's unique perspectives, knowledge, and cultural. We strive to achieve better physical, mental, and spiritual health outcomes through continued connection with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. We understand the need to effectively engage with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities to influence decision making at all levels and to create opportunity through sustainable and culturally safe employment.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.

Shape how digital change is experienced across one of Australia's largest health services.



About the Service


The Design and Architecture Services Department provides strategic architectural leadership across Monash Health, ensuring digital investments, systems and solutions align with organisational priorities and deliver long-term value. Working closely with clinical, operational and technology stakeholders, the team guides technology strategy, solution design, portfolio management and architectural governance to create a connected, sustainable and future-ready digital ecosystem that supports exceptional patient care and service delivery.



About The Role


If appointed to this business-critical role, you'll provide strategic leadership across enterprise architecture, technology governance, solution design and application portfolio management. 


Leading a team of architects and technical specialists, and reporting to the Director, Digital Applications and Architecture, you'll be responsible for defining the future-state architecture for one of Australia's largest and most complex health services, ensuring digital investments align with clinical, operational and organisational priorities. Working closely with executive leaders, clinicians, technology teams and external partners, you'll establish architecture standards, guide major technology decisions and shape a connected, sustainable and future-ready digital ecosystem.


Success in the role will be measured across four key areas: 



Development and delivery of Monash Health's future-state architecture and technology roadmaps


Establishment of architecture governance, standards and design assurance practices


Application portfolio management, rationalisation and lifecycle planning 


Excellence in stakeholder engagement and development of trusted partnerships across clinical, operational and digital teams



This is a Full Time, ongoing role, based in our hybrid workplace. The importance of connection and relationship development across the business cannot be underestimated and you'll happily work on a Monash Health site at least half of your working week to support your team and drive this important work. Travel across Monash Health sites will be required.



About You


You're a strategic technology leader who sees the bigger picture and brings others on the journey. You recognise that great architecture is about more than technology, it's about aligning digital investments with organisational priorities, enabling innovation, managing risk and creating sustainable foundations for the future.


Equally comfortable influencing executives, collaborating with clinicians and working alongside technical teams to solve complex challenges, you have a strong background in enterprise architecture, digital transformation and technology strategy. In addition, you bring proven ability to translate organisational objectives into pragmatic roadmaps, standards and governance frameworks that deliver measurable value.


An inspiring leader, you build trust readily, creating alignment across diverse stakeholder groups and developing high performing teams. Combining strategic thinking with practical delivery, you're passionate about designing technology ecosystems that improve outcomes for clinicians, consumers and the broader health service.


What you'll bring:



Significant leadership experience in enterprise architecture, technology strategy, solution architecture or digital transformation within a large, complex organisation


Strong understanding of modern architecture practices, including cloud platforms, integration patterns, APIs, data ecosystems security, risk and compliance


Demonstrated experience developing architecture roadmaps, governance frameworks, standards and design assurance practices that support strategic technology investment


Proven success leading high-performance specialist teams and navigating organisational change within complex or highly regulated environments


Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across executive, clinical, operational and technical environments



Tertiary qualifications in Information Technology, Computer Science, Digital Health or a related discipline will be highly regarded.



Why Join Design and Architecture Services at Monash Health


Take advantage of a rare opportunity to shape and influence enterprise-wide technology strategy, drive digital transformation and play a key role in enabling the delivery of safer, connected and more sustainable healthcare. Working at the intersection of clinical care, technology and innovation, you'll help create smarter digital solutions that improve patient outcomes and support the clinicians who deliver them every day




At Monash Health, you will:




Work within a values-driven, purpose-led organisation 


Be part of a connected network of clinical, academic and system leaders 


Help drive innovation, inclusion and better health outcomes





We offer:




The opportunity to make a real impact on patient experience


A supportive, collaborative team environment


Ongoing learning and development opportunities


The chance to be part of Victoria's largest public health service




For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Victoria Hornidge, Director, Digital Applications, on 0425 728 838



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation,

Locations	 South Brisbane, QLD, 4101
Full-Time	 Immediate start
Reports to	 Manager
Job Title	 Trade Waiter
Salary range	 $79,500 - $90,000 + Superannuation – depending on skill level
Job Closure date	 30 days

About Our Client
Our client is an award-winning luxury hotel, renowned as a vibrant and sophisticated urban destination. This dynamic precinct is a celebrated hub where luxury accommodation meets an exclusive collection of high-end retail, award-winning restaurants, and stylish bars. The culinary philosophy is centred on creating immersive, memorable experiences through innovative, produce-driven cuisine and impeccable service in a stylish and energetic atmosphere. They are seeking a dedicated Food & Beverage Attendant who embodies this modern, sophisticated ethos to deliver exceptional service in their acclaimed dining venues.

About the Role
We are recruiting on behalf of our client for a passionate and skilled Food & Beverage Attendant (Trade Waiter) to join the dynamic team within their flagship restaurant. This role is the backbone of the guest dining experience, requiring a keen eye for detail, a warm and engaging personality, and a deep commitment to service excellence. You will be responsible for guiding guests through their culinary journey, from the initial greeting to the final farewell, ensuring every interaction reflects the venue’s reputation for sophistication and energy.

Key Responsibilities & Duties
Beverage Service & Sales Enhancement
• Skillfully open bottles at the table and pour beverages, including wine, beer, and non-alcoholic drinks, adhering to professional service standards and enhancing the sense of occasion for guests.
• Proactively monitor and maintain guest tables, promptly removing empty bottles and used glasses, and refilling water and other beverages to ensure an uninterrupted and attentive service flow.
• Confidently recommend wines from our curated list to complement specific food selections, developing your knowledge to expertly pair flavours and enhance the overall culinary experience for our guests.

Operational Excellence & Venue Presentation
• Meticulously set and arrange tables prior to service, ensuring all cutlery, glassware, and tableware are polished, correctly positioned, and meet the highest standards of presentation for a luxury venue.
• Efficiently clear tables between courses, returning dishes and cutlery to the kitchen, and swiftly resetting tables to the pristine standard required for the next seating without disrupting the ambient atmosphere.
• Accurately process guest payments by operating the point-of-sale system and cash register, handling all financial transactions with integrity and providing guests with a smooth and efficient conclusion to their visit.

Candidate Profile & Requirements
• Previous experience in a similar food and beverage service role, preferably within a high-volume, à la carte or fine-dining environment.
• A genuine passion for delivering exceptional customer service with a warm, confident, and engaging personality.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build instant rapport with guests and work seamlessly within a team.
• A strong interest in food, wine, and beverage trends, with a willingness to learn and develop knowledge of menu items and wine pairings.
• Impeccable personal presentation and a professional demeanour that aligns with a luxury brand.
• The ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced environment, maintaining composure and a high attention to detail under pressure.
• Flexibility to work across a rotating roster, including evenings, weekends, and public holidays.

To Apply
If you are a hospitality professional with a passion for delivering unforgettable guest experiences, we invite you to apply. Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your interest in this role.

Please note: All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality. We are acting as the exclusive recruitment partner for this role and our client's identity will be disclosed to shortlisted candidates.
